chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, he said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The time of salat enters upon me while I am traveling, so should I not pray until I enter upon my family? He said: Pray and complete the salat. I said: Then the time of salat enters upon me while I am among my family and I intend to travel, so should I not pray until I go out? He said: Then pray and shorten, for if you do not do so, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

So this does not conflict with the reports we presented earlier, because the way to reconcile them is that whoever returns from his travel while enough time remains for him to complete his salat, completion is required of him; but if he fears missing the time, shortening is required of him. Likewise, whoever sets out on a journey and fears that the time will expire shortens; but if there is sufficient time for him, he completes. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.أَتِمَّ: perform in complete form, without shortening
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: the ruling of shortening the prayer
key_terms.التَّمَامُ: the ruling of full completion of the prayer
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel that affects the legal form of salat
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as the source of normative sunnah
key_terms.قَصِّرْ: perform the salat in shortened form during travel
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: the appointed time of the ritual prayer

ai.seo_question: If the time of salat enters while traveling or just before departure, should one pray full or shortened?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of salat when its time enters at the threshold between residence and travel. It establishes that the duty depends on one’s operative state in relation to travel and the amount of time remaining, and it emphasizes conformity to the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
